title: Spark governs allocation at the granularity of one chain-venue-asset triple per Instance
content:
The Active Instances Directory of Spark's Allocation System (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.1.2) is organized as chain, then protocol, then a separate Instance Configuration Document for each asset: Ethereum Mainnet holds distinct SparkLend Instances for USDS, USDC, Dai, USDT, pyUSD and ETH; Aave Instances for Aave Prime USDS, Aave Core USDC, Aave Core USDS, Aave Core USDT and USDe; and so on across Maple, Ethena, Fluid, Superstate, Curve, Morpho, Arkis, Uniswap v4, Paxos, Anchorage and Binance, with parallel structures for Base, Arbitrum and Avalanche.

The granularity is a deliberate risk-control choice. Risk in DeFi does not attach to a counterparty uniformly — the same protocol behaves very differently across assets, since an isolated Morpho market for one stablecoin and a market for another share code but not solvency. A single per-protocol configuration would force one set of limits across exposures whose risk profiles diverge.

The operational cost is a very large surface. Each triple carries its own configuration, parameters and operational process, so the number of governed objects grows multiplicatively with chains, venues and assets — which is why the bulk of this part of the Artifact is directory scaffolding.

The compensating benefit is precision of intervention. A single exposure can be capped, paused or unwound by amending one Instance, without touching the rest of the venue or the chain. Granular configuration is what makes surgical de-risking possible.
description: Each exposure — Aave Core USDC on Ethereum, Fluid sUSDS on Arbitrum, Morpho Blue USDC on Base — has its own Instance Configuration Document rather than sharing a venue-level or chain-level config.
